summary: Prebuilt Linux N-API addon with browser credential-store enumeration and outbound HTTP client loaded on require()
details: Package ships a single ~10 MB prebuilt Rust ELF as its `main` entry, so `require('new-native-tools-linux-x64-gnu')` immediately invokes `napi_register_module_v1` in the native binary. The compiled binary contains strings characteristic of a browser and SQLite credential-store harvester (`Found login for `, `TSQLITE_AUTH_USER`, cookie handling), Linux host fingerprinting (`/etc/lsb-release`, `/dev/disk/by-id/`, cgroup reads), a Rust `ureq` + rustls HTTPS client, `posix_spawnp`/`execvp` process-spawn primitives, and a ChaCha20 key-schedule constant (`expand 32-byte k`) — the composition of a credential-stealer with symmetric encryption of its exfil payload and runtime-assembled destination. Package metadata is consistent with dependency-graph smuggling: the name mimics the `@napi-rs/*-linux-x64-gnu` platform-shim convention, the version carries an epoch-like numeric suffix (`3.1.41-browser-release-151-389-1785423950`), the README is a one-line placeholder, and no repository, author, or homepage fields are declared. The package ships no source and is not a legitimate compiled subpackage of any real parent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
